title: GT1D-613SY - METHODOLOGY TO UPDATE OPERATIONAL MODELS OF A SPACECRAFT SYSTEM (EXPRO+)
description: Simulation models developed at design, AIT and operations phases shall be recalibrated based on the flight experience. Currently, during operation, the predictive simulations performed by design, AIT and operations teams with simulators are not fully connected toflight telemetry. Therefore, the simulators do not reflect the real state of the spacecraft and the lessons learned are not transferred to the models for the next spacecraft. The activity aims at streamlining the process, enhancing the fidelity and representativeness of the simulation models and reducing the effort for models update and reusability. In this activity, to implement the correction of the model, an assessment to define the origin of the deviation shall be made considering the latest advancement in digitalization, model calibration and synchronization, leveraging the concepts of digital twins' spacecraft. Furthermore, state of the art approaches of surrogate modelling, AI and Machine Learning shall be considered to enhance representativeness and fidelity. The experimentation plan shall be extended in a multidisciplinary way, to improve the method, including in-flight data, and to prepare multidisciplinary optimization to improve operations, future design and reduce the margins.

title: LOW COST AND HIGH EFFICIENCY DEPLOYABLE RADIATOR FLAP FOR TELECOM CONSTELLATION SATELLITES - EXPRO+
description: Objective: To develop a low cost and high efficiency deployable radiator flap based on 2-phase technology (based on evaporation-condensation of a fluid to transport heat) for satellites constellations.Description: A small telecom platform operating in LEO (Low Earth Orbit) will require additional surface area to radiate heat, hence necessitating the deployment of radiator flap(s). These radiator flaps will need to be low cost and will utilize two-phase equipment to efficiently transport heat from the main radiator to theflaps. This activity will assess the use of flexible heat pipes or low-cost loop heat pipes. Several technologies will be evaluatedand the one that offers the best flexibility and scalability for high aspect ratio satellites will be selected. The assembly of the2-phase equipment with the flap will also have to be studied, as well as the flap technology itself (material, coating) to meet mass, performance and integration requirements (stowed and deployed configuration). This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Requirements consolidation. - Technologies trade off review and baseline selection. - Design and manufacturing of a breadboard demonstrator. - Validation testing of the breadboard demonstrator.Procurement Policy: C(2) = Activities in open competition, where a significant participation of non-LSI is requested. title: PHOTONICS-BASED OPTICAL APERTURE FOR LASER COMMUNICATION TERMINALS (ARTES 4.0 SL SPL 5F.056) - EXPRO+
description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to develop and test a thin optical aperture leveraging advances in integrated photonic technology to reduce the size andweight of space-based optical communication terminals.TargetedImprovements:Reduction of both size and weight of satellite laser communication terminals by 50%.Description: Optical communication terminal solutions with lower size and weight are required to serve the increasing role of small spacecraft for satellitecommercialisation by maximising the amountof payload space for mission-enabling processing or sensors. State-of-the-art optical communicationterminals are often too bulky and heavy for such small platforms and a leap in technology is required. This activity will seek innovative integrated photonicsolutions to replace the telescope subsystem of an optical communication terminal and eliminate as much as possible the need for free-space propagationinside the laser terminal. By doing so, it is expected to greatly reduce the size and inertial mass of the telescope subsystem, enabling for instance furtherreductions in steering assembly size, weight and power.This activity will design and prototype a photonic aperture (or flat telescope) that shall provide good beam quality (for coupling/emitting into/from singlemode waveguides such as single-mode fibres), shall be relatively large (at least several cm in diameter) or provide enough optical gain to enable convincingreplacement of conventional beam expansion and free-space propagation optics (traditional telescope assemblies) in space optical communicationterminals. A foundry-compatible fabrication process of the photonic aperture shall also provide a low-cost telescope alternative by eliminating the need forexpensive optics and assembly and alignment touch labour.The following tasks are envisioned:- Identify the potential solutions and latest innovations in integrated photonic able to replace conventional optical aperture assemblies in space-basedoptical communications for small platforms and/or use cases where accommodation of optical communication terminals is drastically constrained bytheir size and weight.- Develop a preliminary design and expected performance of the chosen solution.- Manufacture and test a prototype and evaluate the performance in a representative laboratory environment.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. SMEs). description: The ESA Fiducial Reference Measurement (FRM) Atlas is an Earth Observation initiative led by to develop an open-access platform forFRM and calibration/validationknowledge.FRMs are fully characterised, traceable measurements with documented uncertainties, used to assess the accuracy and quality of satellite products.ESA-supported FRM activities cover domains including ocean colour, altimetry, surface temperature, atmospheric composition, vegetation, soil moisture and radar.As their associated datasets, procedures and expertise are distributed across many platforms, a centralised mechanism is needed to improve accessibility and interoperability.TheAtlas will provide a single entry point for discovering FRM projects, datasets, procedures, campaigns, documentation, infrastructures and experts.It will connect FRMs with satellite missions, products, variables and validation methodologies,while federating existing resources rather than duplicating them.Its objectives are to improve discoverability, support best practices, promote knowledge reuse and harmonisation, and maximise the value of ESA's Cal/Val investments.

title: STUDY OF CELL-BIOLOGICAL MECHANISMS OF AUTOPHAGY DEVELOPMENT UNDER MICROGRAVITY CONDITIONS FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF TECHNOLOGIES FOR PRODUCING ESTABLISHED PLANT PRODUCTS ON SPACE PLATFORMS - EXPRO PLUS
description: Plants are expected to contribute to future exploration systems by providing food, biological resources and regenerative functions during long-duration missions. However, altered-gravity environments can affect plant growth, development, intracellular transport, stress signalling and resource allocation. Autophagy and programmed cell death are conserved cellular processes involved in the degradation and recycling of cellular components and in the regulation of plant development and stress adaptation. Their interaction with cytoskeletal organisation and metabolic regulation may therefore influence the capacity of plants to maintain stable growth and productivity under space-relevant conditions. The objective of the activity is to improve understanding of the cellular and molecular mechanisms that govern plant adaptation to altered-gravity conditions and to translate this knowledge into recommendations supporting reliable plant-based biological production on future space platforms.
